In the opening 20 minutes of the match, both sides played with considerable intensity. After the "water break," each team had a player shown a yellow card – England's midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina's centre-back Lisandro Martínez. By the end of the first half, almost every whistle prompted cheers from fans backing their own side and jeers at the opposition's fouls.

The two sides were level at half-time, but after the change of ends in the second half, England's Anthony Gordon received a pass in the 55th minute to break the deadlock, opening a 1-0 lead that sent England fans across the venue into immediate celebration.

After falling behind, Argentina surged forward in pursuit. Within 10 minutes, they mounted three attacks built around crosses from the right, all of which were blocked, drawing sighs from many Argentina supporters. It was not until the 85th minute that Enzo Fernández headed in a pass from Messi to level the scores at 1-1, sending Argentina fans into delirium with drumming and blaring horns.

In stoppage time, in the 92nd minute, Messi provided the assist and Lautaro Martínez struck the decisive blow against England, sending Argentina through to the final to contest the FIFA World Cup Trophy with Spain. Argentina fans in attendance erupted once more, embracing and celebrating wildly as the final whistle blew. Some lifted Messi cut-out signs from the shopping mall in celebration.

Argentina fan Ah Ho said he had been a Messi supporter ever since the latter emerged from Barcelona. Wearing Argentina's number 10 "two-star" jersey, he noted that this World Cup was Messi's last, as he was also defending the title. His idol Messi and the team had sparked plenty of debate during the tournament, but Ah Ho believed that rather than getting bogged down over refereeing decisions in every match, it was better to cherish Messi's final outings in the national shirt. Laughing, he added, "While I'm still young enough to take it," he had chosen to stay up and watch at the shopping mall with other fans, saying the atmosphere was even better than watching at home. In the end, the result went his way as Argentina advanced to the final.

England fans had been chanting "Football's coming home!" throughout this tournament, but their side fell short of bringing football home this time. Declan, who is studying in the UK, returned to Hong Kong during the summer holiday. Today, draped in the England flag, he got fully behind his side with friends throughout the intense contest. He said this was his first time watching at a shopping mall to soak up the atmosphere, and felt that while the fans were passionate, they also respected each other, with no incidents of serious conflict.

When your team loses, disappointment is inevitable. Declan – who shares his name with England midfielder Declan Rice – felt that England had put in a decent performance in this match. A fan for two tournaments now, he said bluntly, "We've waited 60 years – waiting another four is no big deal!"

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th in pursuit of defending the title, while in the third-place playoff England will take on France on the 19th.
